name.name: Flagellar hook capping protein - N-terminal region

description.text: FlgD is known to be absolutely required for hook assembly, yet it has not been detected in the mature flagellum [[cite:PUB00008482]]. It appears to act as a hook-capping protein to enable assembly of hook protein subunits [[cite:PUB00008482]]. FlgD regulates the assembly of the hook cap structure to prevent leakage of hook monomers into the medium and hook monomer polymerisation and also plays a role in determination of the correct hook length, with the help of the FliK protein [[cite:PUB00109199]]. This family represents the N-terminal conserved region of FlgD. A recent crystal structure showed that this region was likely to be flexible and was cleaved off during crystallisation [[cite:PUB00050852]].
